summary: Trickerion is a heavy worker-placement game where you juggle a team of differently-abled workers to gather components and rehearse tricks, then cash them in via a tense tile-laying performance minigame at the Theater. The performance mechanic is the highlight, rewarding planning and adaptability, but the rest of the game is a long, fiddly build-up of resource and blueprint management.
praised: The Theater performance minigame is tense, clever, and genuinely different from typical worker placement
Strong player asymmetry via unique Illusionist powers and customizable teams
High production value and thematic component design (workshop board, trick tiles)
Rewarding long-term planning as you build toward big performances
criticised: Long playtime and heavy downtime, especially with 4 players and simultaneous action selection resolution
Steep rules overhead and fiddly bookkeeping (component tracking, worker assignment) for the payoff
Snowballing/leader problems can make catch-up difficult once someone gets an efficient trick engine going
Can feel more like a puzzle/engine to optimize solo than a game with rich player interaction outside the Theater

interaction.kind: worker placement blocking plus direct tile-laying conflict during Theater performances

win_criteria: Most points, one or two sources

scoring.why: Fame from successfully performing tricks (with a coin cushion) is essentially the whole game, so the winner is whoever executes the biggest, best-timed performances
